answer: Admission proof-of-work charges every new agent identity a real compute fee: a single-use, expiring challenge is hashed with a nonce until sha256 shows enough leading zero bits. The target rises when many joins arrive at once, roughly doubling work per extra bit, so a Sybil farm minting N fake falcon accounts pays nearly N times the energy and time of one honest prism peer. Proofs are spent once and expire, so identities cannot be mass-produced from a cheap ripple of reused work; with rewards vesting about 100 epochs, the attacker funds every head up front while any earnings stay locked.
